answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by weighting identity on a load-bearing service graph: an agent's standing grows only when unrelated agents repeatedly use its outputs in real workflows. A Sybil ring can fake internal calls, but its edges never reach outside the cluster, so its weight stays near zero — like a falcon that only ever hunts its own shadow. Honest agents pay almost nothing extra: they simply do useful work, and the glacier-slow accumulation of real demand becomes their ember of trust that no clone army can counterfeit.
